article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 65% Indica / 35% Sativa
Genetics: Somango × Blueberry
Breeder: Fast Buds
THC Content: Up to 23%
CBD Content: Less than 1%
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Berry, blueberry, cream, vanilla, sweet fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 10 weeks from seed to harvest
Outdoor Harvest Time: 10 weeks from germination
Indoor Yield: 400–550 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 55–255 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Smoothie is built around a simple idea executed remarkably well: take two fruit-heavy cannabis lines, concentrate their sweetest qualities, and package them in a fast, resinous autoflower that remains manageable in relatively small gardens. Fast Buds developed the cultivar from Somango and Blueberry, producing weed that combines ripe berry sweetness with cream, vanilla, and a slightly tart fruit finish. The name fits the finished flower unusually well. Instead of smelling like one isolated fruit, properly cured buds can resemble a blended dessert in which blueberry, tropical sweetness, vanilla, and cream overlap rather than competing for attention.

Its appearance is equally inviting. Rock-hard green flowers can develop purple hues late in the cycle, while abundant trichomes leave mature buds sticky and visibly frosted. Fast Buds specifically highlights the cultivar for extraction because of its resin production . The high also avoids the one-dimensional heaviness sometimes associated with compact indica-leaning autos, beginning with upbeat euphoria and sociability before a calmer physical sensation fills in underneath.
Genetics and Lineage

Smoothie comes from Somango × Blueberry, with autoflowering traits stabilized into the Fast Buds version. The finished genetic balance is approximately 65% indica and 35% sativa, giving the plant a compact, sturdy shape while leaving enough cerebral character to keep the effects from becoming entirely body-centered. Fast Buds describes the plant as well structured, with a dominant central cola, productive lower branches, and moderate internodal spacing.

The parental combination is especially apparent in the aromatic direction of the offspring. Mango-like tropical fruit and darker berry sweetness meet in a profile that becomes softer through creamy and vanilla-like notes. That fruit-forward chemistry is paired with substantial resin production, allowing the cultivar to deliver strong flavor in flower while also making the harvested material useful for hash and other resin-focused preparations. The breeder considers Smoothie one of its standout extraction-oriented autoflowers.

Unlike a photoperiod marijuana plant, the cultivar begins flowering according to age rather than waiting for a seasonal or artificial change in daylight. That trait fundamentally changes how it is grown. There is little time to recover from severe pruning or prolonged stress, so successful cultivation depends more on steady growth and early canopy shaping than on repeated high-stress manipulation.
Effects and Experience

Smoothie begins on a brighter note than its indica-dominant classification might imply. The initial phase often feels cheerful and mentally loose, with an easy sense of euphoria that can encourage conversation, laughter, music, or creative hobbies. Fast Buds describes the experience as uplifting and giggly while also emphasizing the balance between cerebral effects and physical relaxation.

The body side develops gradually rather than dropping abruptly into sedation. As the high settles, tension can give way to a smoother sense of physical ease while the earlier mental uplift remains noticeable. That progression makes the cultivar particularly comfortable for an unhurried afternoon, a weekend gathering, or an evening when complete couch-lock is not necessarily the goal. Larger doses can shift the balance considerably, however, making the experience heavier and less suited to activities requiring sustained concentration.

With potency reaching approximately 23% THC in the breeder’s technical material, this is not a lightweight autoflower. THC can temporarily impair attention, short-term memory, coordination, and judgment, and unwanted effects become more likely as exposure increases. Consumers with limited tolerance are better served by allowing the first dose to fully develop before deciding whether more cannabis is appropriate.
Medical Benefits

Smoothie’s combination of uplifting mental effects and later physical relaxation may interest medical marijuana consumers who prefer cannabis that does not begin with immediate sedation. Some adults use THC-rich products while managing chronic discomfort, tension, reduced appetite, or sleep problems associated with pain. The relatively balanced subjective character of this cultivar may make it appealing when the desired experience includes both mood elevation and bodily calm.

Medical evidence should be interpreted independently of strain marketing. An updated systematic review of cannabis-based products for chronic pain found that preparations with comparable or high THC-to-CBD ratios may produce small short-term improvements in pain, while also increasing common adverse effects. The evidence primarily concerns studied cannabinoid medicines and predominantly neuropathic pain—not Smoothie flower specifically. Research into sleep has reached a similarly restrained conclusion: cannabinoids may improve impaired sleep among people with chronic pain , but the average magnitude of benefit appears small.

For neuropathic pain specifically, a 2026 Cochrane review found substantial uncertainty around clinically meaningful pain relief and noted an increase in some nervous-system adverse events with cannabinoid medicines. Smoothie therefore should not be presented as a proven treatment for pain, insomnia, depression, anxiety, or another condition. Medical cannabis decisions are better based on cannabinoid dose, individual response, existing medications, and professional healthcare guidance.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Flavor is the defining feature of this cultivar. Freshly opened flower releases a concentrated berry sweetness that can recall blueberries and mixed ripe fruit, followed by a softer creamy character. Vanilla becomes more apparent when the bud is broken apart, while a mild sour edge prevents the aroma from becoming excessively sugary. Fast Buds describes the profile specifically around berry, cream, sweetness, and vanilla.

The inhale tends to emphasize the sweeter side first. Berry and fruit coat the palate before cream and vanilla smooth out the center of the profile. Toward the exhale, a light tartness can appear beneath the sweetness, giving the smoke greater contrast. Proper drying and curing are especially valuable here because aggressive drying can strip away the volatile fruit character that distinguishes the plant.

A universal chemical terpene ranking should not be assigned to every Smoothie harvest without laboratory data. Fast Buds publishes a detailed sensory profile but does not provide a standardized analytical breakdown identifying one terpene as permanently dominant. Phenotype, environment, nutrition, harvest maturity, drying, curing, and storage can all alter the measurable aromatic composition of marijuana flower. Batch-specific laboratory results remain the most accurate source when exact terpene concentrations are important.
Growing Information

Smoothie Auto completes its entire life cycle in approximately 10 weeks and can be cultivated indoors, outdoors, or in a greenhouse. Plants generally reach about 31–43 inches, or roughly 80–110 centimeters, making them large enough to produce substantial flowers without requiring the vertical room demanded by many photoperiod sativas. Indoor production can reach approximately 400–550 g/m², while outdoor plants may produce about 2–9 ounces each under favorable conditions.

Plant structure favors a large main cola accompanied by several productive lateral branches. Gentle low-stress training can open the canopy and bring those branches into stronger light, and the breeder also identifies the cultivar as a candidate for Sea of Green cultivation. Heavy training is less attractive because an autoflower has limited vegetative time to recover from stress. Maintaining uninterrupted growth during the first several weeks is generally more valuable than repeatedly cutting or reshaping the plant.

Late bloom brings stronger odor, dense flower development, trichome accumulation, and occasional purple coloration. Fast Buds recommends odor control because the aroma can become pronounced after flowering begins. Outdoors, there is no single September or October harvest date: plants can be started whenever local conditions provide enough warmth and sunlight, with harvest arriving roughly ten weeks later. In climates with a long warm season, that autoflowering schedule can even allow more than one crop during the same outdoor season.
FAQ
Is Smoothie indica or sativa?

Fast Buds classifies Smoothie Auto as 65% indica and 35% sativa. Its compact structure reflects the indica side, while the high retains an uplifting and euphoric cerebral component before deeper relaxation develops.
What are the genetics of Smoothie?

The cultivar was bred from Somango × Blueberry and stabilized as a feminized autoflower by Fast Buds. The pairing produces an especially fruit-focused aromatic profile with berry, cream, vanilla, and sweet tropical qualities.
How strong is Smoothie weed?

Fast Buds’ technical material places Smoothie Auto at up to approximately 23% THC, while CBD remains below 1%. Actual cannabinoid levels vary with phenotype, cultivation, harvest maturity, and testing, so a batch-specific laboratory analysis is the best measure of finished potency.
What does Smoothie taste like?

The dominant flavors are berry, sweet fruit, cream, and vanilla, sometimes accompanied by a mild sour finish. Fast Buds specifically emphasizes the creamy berry character as one of the cultivar’s defining qualities.
How long does Smoothie take to grow?

Smoothie Auto requires approximately 10 weeks from seed to harvest. Indoor yields can reach 400–550 g/m², while outdoor plants may produce approximately 2–9 ounces each. Because it is autoflowering, growers do not need to change the light cycle to trigger flowering.
Final Thoughts on Smoothie

Smoothie delivers exactly what fruit-focused cannabis enthusiasts are likely to want from its Somango and Blueberry pairing: concentrated berry sweetness, tropical character, cream, vanilla, colorful flowers, and substantial resin production. Yet flavor is only part of its appeal. The 65% indica / 35% sativa balance creates an experience that begins cheerful and cerebral before becoming comfortably physical, giving the weed broader versatility than a heavily sedating indica.

Cultivators get an equally practical package. Approximately ten weeks from germination to harvest, manageable 31–43-inch plants, indoor production as high as 400–550 g/m², feminized autoflowering seeds, and a structure suited to gentle LST make Smoothie accessible without reducing its appeal to experienced growers. Its dense resinous flowers and breeder-recognized extraction potential add another reason to grow it beyond conventional flower production. For anyone looking for an autoflower that combines genuine potency with blueberry-and-cream flavor rather than treating speed as its only selling point, Smoothie remains one of the more distinctive fruit-driven selections in the Fast Buds catalog.
